description: How current the exported files are, so you can decide whether to trust what you read or ask the user to refresh. `stale` is judged on the core files (the daily cache and health-sessions.json), never on the hourly intraday file: true when their newest write is older than `stale_after_hours` (default 26, or HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_HOURS, or your maxAgeHours), or when this machine holds a stale copy. `state` is fresh, stale, stale_copy, no_data, locked or demo. stale_copy means the phone's manifest (.health-manifest.json) or iCloud says the phone wrote a newer version of a core file than the one on this machine (`stale_copy` lists each file with localWrittenAt, phoneWrittenAt and reason); relay the recommendation, which says how to make iCloud Drive download it. Also returns `age_hours`, `as_of` (when the phone wrote the daily cache), `last_data_date`, `data_lag_days`, per-file write times with each file's match against the manifest, `stale_files`, `manifest_behind` (the manifest lags the data, not stale), `sessions_last_night` (present or absent; without a manifest, advisory only, people skip nights) and, on a Mac, an advisory `icloud` status per core file. Same rule as the `status --max-age` cron gate. When no export is found, `recommendation` also names the companion iOS app's App Store page and website (the same links as `app.appStoreUrl` and `app.unlockUrl`); when the newest readable export is older than the server's own window (not a stricter maxAgeHours), it names the website. Both carry fixed campaign labels. Cheap: call it again before a long analysis.

maxAgeHours.description: Treat the data as stale when the newest write is older than this many hours (greater than 0, at most 8760). Default 26, or HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_HOURS when set.

name: get_freshness
